newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Brent supports say up but charts top-out.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Brent supports say up but charts top-out.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
*A long legged near doji candlestick formation on the Brent chart which following Friday's long white candlestick could be read as a sign that this current uptrend has topped out.
*The fact that supports held under pressure on Tuesday may see the market again taking a look at Friday's $20.60 a barrel high, technical analysts said.
Intact chart supports on Brent and gas oil futures point the market high but Japanese charting techniques and weakening crack spreads may push crude lower, brokers and analysts said.

On Tuesday the Brent market dipped in early trade anticipating pressure from the expiring June NYMEX contract but both IPE and NYMEX contracts pulled back from the lows towards the close after earlier falling to breach supports.
This left a long legged near doji candlestick formation on the Brent chart which following Friday's long white candlestick could be read as a sign that this current uptrend has topped out.
"It's a bit of an uncertain pattern but the doji is similar to that of March 19 after which the market dipped to $17.54," said Steve Kwan at Standard and Poor's MMS International.
"It's pretty balanced at the moment holding the $20.50 high of mid-March but if we do see a break lower $19.50 may prove a significant support level," Kwan added.

Brokers said the fact that supports held under some pressure on Tuesday may see the market again taking a look at Friday's $20.60 a barrel high with SIMEX trading 13 cents up at $20.13 and NYMEX crude up 16 cents from the close at around $21.75 in overnight ACCESS trade following a draw in U.S. stocks.
They said the $20.84 a barrel high of March 19 may also be targeted but that the Jan 9 high of $24.91 seemed a long way off.
The 14-day RSI is turning lower in the neutral zone and the 10/20 day moving average lines holding below the mid-$19 level and widening out.
Fundamentally weakening crack spreads could also put some pressure on crude causing prices to drift lower.

Gas oil's gap up on the front-month continuation chart from $173 last Friday to $176.50 on Monday was partially closed on Tuesday but strength on the close left the effects of its support intact and may allow the market to ignore a modest U.S. stock build, analysts say.
The market has ended above the Monday's $176.75 high for the past two days with supports holding well. Brokers said the next target may now be the $183.75 high of February 14.
However, the 14-day RSI crept further towards the overbought region and moving averages are still the low $170s and showing little sign of a bullish 10/20-day cross.
NYMEX crude rose moderately in thin ACCESS trade, supported by new data on Tuesday that showed a draw in nationwide crude stocks.

Traders said ACCESS prices reacted slowly to the weekly inventory report from the American Petroleum Institute. The trade group said crude on hand at U.S. refiners dropped a sharp 5.9 million barrels.

"There wasn't much of a reaction initially," one trader said, noting the new front-month contract, July, rose as high as $21.80 a barrel before slipping back to $21.75, about 16 cents a barrel over the daytime close.
Traders saw crude oil resistance at $22.15 on Wednesday, with support at $21.50 a barrel.
June heating oil fell 0.16 cent a gallon after-hours to 57.80 cents. June unleaded gasoline eased to 65.35 a gallon, off a mere 0.04 cent from the settle.
-- Colin Wooster, London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7456
